title_guess: Reserve ratios CRR and SLR: how they work, legal limits, history, SLR securities and today's split of NDTL
recurring_cast: red down-arrows each passing a red % sign
vault (gold CRR box with a safe door, held by RBI)
small_safe (grey SLR safe kept by the bank)
law_document (act icon; an 'Amend 2007' version with a pencil)
three-row rule table (CRR range, interest on CRR, SLR range)
running_examples: today: CRR 4.5% + SLR 18% of NDTL, so 77.5% is left for lending
legal band shown on screen: CRR 3-15% of NDTL, changed in 2007 to 'up to 15%'; SLR 25-40%, changed to 'up to 40%'

best_moments.why: a red arrow from the bank's NDTL passes a % sign and lands in a gold vault held by the RBI coin, marked cash and 0% interest: 'part of deposits locked with RBI, earning nothing' in one picture
an 'Amend 2007' law tag sends a dotted arrow to the legal range '3% to 15%', which is struck and rewritten as 'up to 15%': a law change shown on the number it changes
a second arrow from the same NDTL drops into a grey safe that stays with the bank (not RBI): one source, two destinations, which is the CRR vs SLR difference
the opening picture returns with today's numbers (4.5%, 18%) and a third arrow 'available for lending 77.5%' from which a row of small arrows rains down onto a crowd of borrowers
CRR history curve with a grey band on the 1991 peak and a reform committee icon sending a red arrow to that band: who acted at which turning point
compliance loop: 'maintain (mandatory)' arc over the reserve card, a fortnightly report rising to RBI, and a dotted penalty line looping back down to the bank

weak_moments.why: six kinds of eligible SLR securities as a long blue text list, written on line by line for about a minute
the rule table is built cell by cell for about 100 s; it is a text table, useful as a summary but slow
the reason for SLR (cushion for withdrawals) is a paragraph callout, not shown as depositors withdrawing from the safe

act labels on screen should be verified before BIE reuses any of it: both reserves are tagged with a 1949 'RBI Act', while CRR is usually cited under the RBI Act 1934 and SLR under the Banking Regulation Act 1949; the legal bands shown may also need checking

segments.teaches: a bank must keep a share of its net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) as cash with RBI (CRR); RBI pays 0% on it (interest stopped in 2007); RBI decides the rate within a legal band shown as 3-15%, which a 2007 amendment changed to 'up to 15%'

red down-arrow to a red %, then a diagonal line down to the CRR box
gold rectangle labelled CRR with a safe door, attached to the RBI coin, 'cash' under it
RBI emblem coin with letters RBI
'0% interest' over the vault
box under RBI: interest used to be paid, stopped from 2007
law icon with '3% to 15%' feeding the % sign
blue 'decides' elbow from RBI up to the range
'Amend 2007' tag with a pencil icon, dotted arrow to the range
'3% to 15%' struck, 'up to 15%' written above

segments.notes: 8 change events (~every 9 s). Verify before reuse: the on-screen act name and legal band for CRR (CRR is usually cited under the RBI Act 1934).
segments.idea: a fixed slice of every bank's deposits must sit as cash with RBI, earning nothing, at a rate RBI chooses within the law
segments.shown_as: bank icon on top with its NDTL label; a red arrow drops to a % sign and runs down into a gold vault held by the RBI coin, marked cash and 0% interest; a law icon writes '3% to 15%' into the % and a blue 'decides' arrow links RBI to it; then an 'Amend 2007' tag sends a dotted arrow that strikes the range and writes 'up to 15%' above it
segments.example: CRR band 3-15% of NDTL, after 2007 'up to 15%'; 0% interest

segments.teaches: SLR: a second share of NDTL stays with the bank itself as gold, cash or government securities; it is a cushion so the bank can meet withdrawals

elements.what: second red down-arrow from NDTL through its own % into a grey safe
small grey safe labelled SLR, standing apart from RBI
'gold, cash or G-secs' under the safe
box: cushion against liquidity risk, money for withdrawals

segments.notes: 3 change events in 75 s (~every 25 s). Two parallel arrows from one NDTL = one source, two homes (RBI's vault vs the bank's own safe).
segments.idea: SLR money stays in the bank's own safe in liquid form, ready for depositors
segments.shown_as: a second red arrow drops from NDTL beside the first, through its own % sign, into a small grey safe labelled SLR that stays with the bank, not with RBI; 'gold, cash or G-secs' writes under it and a callout box explains it as a cushion for withdrawals

segments.teaches: unlike CRR, banks earn income on SLR holdings; the law set SLR at 25-40% of NDTL, later changed to 'up to 40%'

elements.what: 'banks earn income on this investment' under the safe, blue underline
law icon at right writing '25% to 40%' into the SLR %
'25% to 40%' struck, 'up to 40%' written above

segments.notes: 4 change events (~every 12 s). The SLR side mirrors the CRR side (law icon, band, strike), so the two reserves read as twins with different homes and yields. Verify the act name for SLR (usually the Banking Regulation Act 1949).
segments.idea: SLR assets earn the bank a return, and SLR has its own legal band
segments.shown_as: under the SLR safe an 'earns income' line is underlined (against CRR's 0%); a law icon on the right writes '25% to 40%' into the SLR % sign, and later that band is struck and 'up to 40%' is written above it, mirroring the CRR change
segments.example: SLR band 25-40% of NDTL, later 'up to 40%'

segments.teaches: summary of the rules by era: CRR band then 'up to 15%'; interest on CRR 'RBI could fix' then 0%; SLR band then 'up to 40%'

elements.what: blue line 1949 - 2007 - now, with a law icon at 1949 and an 'Amend 2007' law icon
three rows (CRR requirement, interest on CRR, SLR requirement) cut into era columns by dotted drop lines from the ticks; SLR row in green
vault and safe icons as row markers at the left

segments.notes: 13 change events (~every 8 s), each one a cell or a label. Era table = timeline ticks cut the table into columns; reusable for any rule change.
segments.idea: what the law allowed before and after 2007, side by side
segments.shown_as: a blue timeline draws from 1949 to now with a law icon at 1949 and an 'Amend 2007' law icon; dotted lines drop from both ticks to cut a table; rows fill cell by cell (CRR band then 'up to 15%', interest 'RBI could fix' then '0%', a green SLR row band then 'up to 40%'), with the vault and safe icons marking their rows

segments.teaches: CRR history: 3% in 1949, 6% in 1978, a 15% peak in 1991, then down to 10% and 4.5% (2003 to 2023); the 1991 reform committee advised 3-5%

elements.what: rule table shrinks into a left strip, its CRR row framed in black
line curve of CRR % over years with yellow dots and value labels; dotted drop lines to the year axis
grey vertical band on the 1991 peak
committee table with five figures, the chair in red, name label above
red arrow from the committee up to the 1991 band
report icon with a tick, 'recommendations', first bullet: CRR 3-5%

segments.notes: 6 change events (~every 6 s). Committee pointing at the peak ties an actor to a turning point in the data.
segments.idea: CRR peaked at 15% in 1991; reformers asked to cut it to 3-5%, and it has fallen since
segments.shown_as: the rule table shrinks to the left with its CRR row framed; at right a line curve draws through dotted year markers, rising to a 15% peak at 1991 and falling to 4.5%; a grey band lights 1991, and a committee table of five figures (chair in red) sends a red arrow to that band while a report icon lists the 3-5% advice

segments.teaches: the committee also said RBI should pay interest on CRR; RBI paid it from 1999 until the 2007 amendment stopped it

grey box: RBI started paying interest on CRR

'Amend 2007' law icon at the bar's end with a 'payment stopped' note
interest row framed in the left table

segments.notes: 5 change events (~every 7 s). The graph clears first; a mini-timeline bar shows a time window cheaply.
segments.idea: interest on CRR was paid only for a short window, 1999 to 2007
segments.shown_as: the graph clears; a second advice bullet writes on, an arrow drops from 'RBI started paying' onto a short blue 1999-2007 bar, and an 'Amend 2007' law icon at the bar's end hooks a 'payment stopped' note; on the left the table's interest row is framed

segments.teaches: SLR history: 20% in 1949, a 38.5% peak in 1991, cut to 25% by 1997, 18% now; the committee asked for 38.5% to 25% over five years

elements.what: SLR % curve over years with labelled points
red translucent circle on the 38.5% peak, later moved to the 25% point
third recommendation bullet: cut SLR to 25% over 5 years
SLR row framed in the left table

segments.notes: 5 change events (~every 10 s). Moving the circle from the 'before' point to the 'after' point shows the cut on the curve itself.
segments.idea: SLR was cut from a 1991 high of 38.5% to 25% within a few years and is lower today
segments.shown_as: an SLR curve draws in at the bottom right; a red circle glows on the 38.5% peak at 1991 as the advice bullet writes on, then the circle jumps down to the 25% point at 1997 to show the cut done; the table's SLR row is framed at left

segments.teaches: banks were allowed to choose their SLR assets; RBI introduced 'SLR securities' in 1996, covering rated corporate bonds, bank CDs, rated NBFC commercial paper, state development loans, multilateral-bank securities and NABARD / SIDBI securities

elements.what: fourth recommendation bullet: banks may pick their liquid assets
curved arrow from the bullet to an 'SLR securities' tag joined to the RBI coin
'introduced in 1996' line
six-item list of eligible securities in blue text

segments.notes: 11 change events (~every 9 s), mostly list lines. Weakest stretch: a long text list with no picture of what each paper is.
segments.idea: SLR can now be held in a wider approved list of safe securities, not only government paper
segments.shown_as: a fourth advice bullet appears and a curved arrow loops from it to an 'SLR securities' tag tied to the RBI coin with '1996'; the panel slides up and a six-item list of eligible paper writes on one line at a time

segments.teaches: today CRR is 4.5% and SLR 18% of NDTL; SLR may be held in G-secs or other SLR securities; the remaining 77.5% is available for lending to people

segments.teaches: CRR and SLR are mandatory reserve ratios; banks send RBI a fortnightly report; failing to maintain them brings a penalty
